points.description: States the purpose: both are broadcast methods that reduce/minimize duplicate packets compared with flooding.

Reverse Path Forwarding: on receiving a packet from source S via neighbor N, node X checks its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all adjacent nodes except N only if N is the next hop X would use to send to S (i.e. packet arrived on the best path); otherwise it discards it.

Reverse Path Broadcast: works like RPF but nodes learn (by monitoring unicast traffic) which spanning-tree/best paths they are part of, and forward only on edges that belong to a spanning tree (excluding the incoming link).
